speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To help me understand the severity, has this swelling been constant, or does it come and go? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Engineer by profession.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, weight loss, trauma to the knee, or previous similar episodes. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very surprising, as a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) typically presents with urinary symptoms rather than isolated knee swelling; could you please clarify what symptoms your previous doctor was treating? In the meantime, please tell me if you have noticed any redness, warmth, or a visible lump on your knee, and have you been able to fully bend or straighten it? REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: Slightly elevated, C-Reactive_Protein: Within normal limits

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an interesting discrepancy; while your ESR is slightly elevated, your CRP is normal, which can sometimes point toward conditions like gout or crystal arthropathy rather than a systemic bacterial infection. Since your previous doctor suggested a UTI, could you tell me if you have noticed any recent urinary symptoms like burning, frequency, or changes in your urine color? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Normal, Urine Culture: Negative growth
